title: The Eye of Allah Watches Over You: The Value of Hidden Deeds
summary:
Have you noticed how your child's behavior changes when they know someone is watching them? Perhaps they tidy their room quickly if they know guests are coming, or they strive to show their best at school when there's an evaluation. This is human nature, to seek to please those we see. But as the teenage years approach, this influence grows, and people's opinions become the primary driver of their actions, potentially making them forget the ultimate goal.

This is where our role as parents comes in: to plant the seed of sincerity in their hearts. To teach them that there is an Eye that neither slumbers nor sleeps, seeing every small and large thing, and that is the Eye of Allah, the Most High. That good deeds are not only what people see and praise, but the most beautiful and precious are those done in secret, where only Allah sees them. This deep value gives them an internal compass that guides them towards good for its own sake, not for people's praise, and makes them a person of firm principle.

Reminding your child that Allah is aware of them at every moment is the most precious gift you can give them. This internal self-monitoring is their trustworthy guardian when you are absent, and their protective shield in a time when temptations and social pressures are abundant. Teach them to seek the pleasure of Allah alone, and to feel His companionship in every action, whether small or large. Make this idea a part of your daily conversations, to build within them an impenetrable fortress of sincerity and truthfulness.
try_this: Tonight: Talk with your child about a good deed they did today that no one saw, and how only Allah knows about it and rewards them for it.
reflection_prompts: How can I instill in my child the love of doing good deeds solely for Allah, away from people's opinions?
What daily situations can I use to reinforce the idea of Allah's awareness in my child's heart?
parent_script: “Remember, my child, that Allah sees everything, even your purest hidden deeds.”
assistant_prompts: How do I deal with my child if I see them doing something good only for others to see?
What activities can encourage my child to perform secret acts of charity?
